cim: How human and artificial intelligence take flight at Airbus to re-invent Supply Chain Management
cim_eredeti: How human and artificial intelligence take flight at Airbus to re-invent Supply Chain Management
szoveg_eredeti:
In an earlier article, Pascal Daloz, CEO of French multi-national Dassault Systèmes, made his pitch for the rise of Industrial Intelligence, “where AI meets industrial reality” to meet the trust and reliability needs of customers in sectors such as aerospace.

One leader in this space is Europe’s Airbus, whose CEO Guillaume Faury argues that the group faces particular competitive pressures:

We are in an industry and in sectors - Civil Aviation, Aerospace, Space itself, helicopters and others - where we enjoy growth, actually a very fast growth. We have more than 10 years of backlog for our commercial aircraft, and we need to ramp up.

But we are also at a point where we are preparing the next generation of products...We are in a situation where the complexity, the size, the complexity of our products is increasing. We are looking at the product not in isolation, but we are looking at the product, the production system that we [use to] manufacture those sophisticated products, and the world of operations when those products will be operated by multiple clients over a long period of time.

This is a set of challenges that the firm is looking to a combination of human and artificial intelligence to address. According to Faury:

We need to bring the intelligence of human beings collaborating together to design and manufacture those products to service them. We need to bring the capabilities of data to use Artificial Intelligence in combination with humans, and this in a rather complex environment over several countries inside Airbus and with our partners outside of Airbus. Nobody can manage that complexity in the sense of what humans can access, so, we need the ability to orchestrate all of this.

Virtual twin tech from Dassault is at the center of its approach to this:

It’s something we can no longer work without. We don't deliver an aircraft or a satellite ‘almost’ complete, we don't deliver an aircraft that is ‘almost’ safe. [We deal with] the level of details and understanding of what we're doing, the level of mastery, the ability to go into the details of objects and production systems, which are very large, distributed all around the world with a high degree of complexity, where we have software and hardware working together, systems connecting with others [and] connected products moving forward.

This can only be made through bringing reality, physical reality, into a digital world where we can assess, we can test, we can compare, we can multiply the number of configurations we are evaluating, and we can get the support of AI to increase the number of possibilities.

That's what we're doing through the digital twin. That's what we're doing with Dassault’s] 3DEXPERIENCE agent platform. There's no product or no production system tomorrow that will exist without having had before its digital twin, its digital brother, on which we will have applied a lot of tests, a lot of experience, a lot of simulation, and it creates the ability to bring much more sophisticated products much faster in a more reliable way.

The commitment to 3DEXPERIENCE is clearly significant and well-established at Airbus itself:

What we have decided to do at Airbus moving forward is to put all our activities on 3DEXPERIENCE. We are doing it on Airbus commercial developments and production systems on helicopters. We have had a good co-operation on helicopters already now for many years, also in the field of defense and space. So, we go across the board.

We go step by step because we need to mature our ability to work with 3DEXPERIENCE. We need also to mature the platform itself as we are moving forward, given the constraints [of] traceability, reliability, cybersecurity, sovereignty. Ultimately, for the products that will enter into the market in the next decade, they will be born, they will be native, on 3DEXPERIENCE, they will be maintained [and] they will be further developed on 3DEXPERIENCE.

But it’s also an evolving strategy as Faury explains:

What is new is the fact that we no longer look at products in isolation, but we look at the product in their production environment, in their industrial environment, and how they are operated along the years in a single source of truth of data that can be accessed by everybody in the same way and going beyond the borders of the company.

This is something that the firm needs to see expand out into its partner ecosystem:

In some cases, we have started doing it together, but we need this going further to most of our main partners and suppliers so that we can expand the potential of this way of working because working in 3DEXPERIENCE gives speed, gives reliability, gives control of what we are doing, and gives this potential for use of AI, meaning doing much more than what we would be doing in a standard way.

There are a few challenges here, including the need to accelerate the ramp-up, but overall the direction of travel is clearly set in:

It’s all about Supply Chain Management and industrial performance, but it's also the preparation of the next generation of products in this new environment.
